post: Every street in OMERTÀ can become a route, a refuge, or a mistake. The city is the board; your choices give it a history.
alt: Rain-soaked rooftops and a harbor at night, with one warmly lit safehouse window overlooking the city.

post: Your first job is small. The question that follows is not: bank the cash, press your luck, or find someone who can keep you alive?
Six districts means six different contexts for the same ambition. Where you stand changes what you can reach, buy, risk, and learn.
A character is dealt a stat spread, not a destiny. Build around the hand you draw and the city starts to look different.
The quietest player in the room may be studying travel time. In OMERTÀ, geography can be as useful as a gun.
Some stories only open on the right street. A map is more than decoration when location changes the available choices.
The opening minutes are a question of nerve: take the standard route, case the job, or go loud and accept the heat.
One life makes preparation matter. The next move can be planned; the city's response belongs to the server.
The streets do not award a perfect build. They give you constraints and ask what kind of criminal you can become inside them.
If the next district offers a better price, the trip still costs time and cash. Opportunity has a route.
The city remembers more than your balance. Standing, reputation, and the people you crossed become part of your position.
An early win is useful. Knowing when to put it in the bank may be more useful.
There is no universal best street. One district may hold a clue; another may hold the buyer; a third may hold the people looking for you.
Your first week has a coach, missions, and daily contracts. Guidance points at the next decision; it does not make it for you.
In OMERTÀ, a ledger can be a weapon of memory. It records what moved even after the person who moved it is gone.
The path from a tiny job to a citywide reputation is made of ordinary choices with consequences that accumulate.
Think like a local: where can you work, who knows your name, and how long will the trip home take?
The same crime can feel different when you case it first. Information is a resource before it becomes an advantage.
Go loud and you may gain speed. You may also gain heat. That tradeoff is the story of a street game.
The next mission is visible. The safest route to it might not be.
OMERTÀ's streets reward curiosity: routes, district prices, cases, and contacts connect in ways a single menu cannot show.
You can become known for a profession, a Path, or the kind of trouble that follows you into a room. Net worth is one signal.
Six Paths offer different methods: Gun, Ledger, Kitchen, Wheel, Shadow, and Ring. The city still belongs to the choices you make.
What would you protect first in a hostile city: your cash, your name, your allies, or your route home?
There is a difference between having a map and knowing the city. The first tells you where; the second tells you why now matters.
You can leave a district. You cannot erase the time and cash spent getting somewhere else.
A small lead can become a long errand chain. The Underworld's named fixtures have standing, favors, grudges, and memory.
The person offering a favor today may remember a slight next week. Relationships are part of the economy.
Your character's strengths begin with a conserved total. Nobody starts with a strictly better body; decisions do the rest.
The city keeps score of honor and infamy. The same action can pay in cash and cost something harder to replace.
One district's opportunity is another district's warning. Read the street before you commit the crew.
The most useful number on your screen might be travel time when a case, buyer, or rival is somewhere else.
OMERTÀ is a place where an ordinary errand can touch a larger feud. The server tracks the consequences after the scene ends.
What does a reputation buy you when the wrong people also know your name?
There are faster ways to work and safer ways to work. A good criminal has to notice when those are different routes.
The first week is a climb with signposts. Your coach can point; only your choices create the record.
If you are planning three moves ahead, start with the district. The city makes timing and distance part of strategy.
Every job is a small argument with uncertainty. Preparation changes the odds; it never turns a roll into a guarantee.
The safest place for cash is not always the most convenient place for it. Where you end a night matters.
Some players collect cars. Others see routes, freight, repair bills, race entries, and escape plans in the same garage.
A garage is a risk ledger on wheels: condition, repairs, boosting, and fencing can turn one vehicle into several decisions.
Your build is not a costume. Skills, respec, capstones, and mastery leave a record of what you chose to practice.
The city's long game includes clues, collections, landmarks, and story flags. A season can end without erasing its history.
The more a place matters to your plan, the more it matters that somebody else can reach it too.
Noir begins with a choice: the envelope on the doorstep, the bank across town, the favor you still owe.
One life changes the tone of every gamble. A prepaid revive may stop a killing blow; succession is what follows a death that lands.
The heir does not inherit a clean slate. Money, enemies, and unfinished business can travel with the bloodline.
OMERTÀ's city is persistent because consequences have addresses: a district, a ledger, a garage, a relationship, a family name.
You do not need a grand plan to enter the city. You do need to decide what kind of risk you are willing to carry.
The invitation door is open at omerta.fun. Explore the streets, learn their rules, and decide where your first night begins.
Six Paths. One city. Gun, Ledger, Kitchen, Wheel, Shadow, and Ring change the methods available to a character; they do not write the ending.
alt: Rain-wet city intersection where six roads diverge into the night.

post: Pick a Path for the kind of problems you want to solve. The streets will still ask you to solve problems outside your specialty.
A Wheel specialist sees a garage as a toolkit. A Ledger specialist sees an opening in the books. Neither gets to ignore the other.
In a city of conserved stat totals, expertise is the answer to a limitation, not an excuse to avoid one.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: DEATH IS FINAL. THE LINE CONTINUES. Revive protection can stop a killing blow. Death starts a succession.

post: The Gun Path is a way of approaching danger. It is not a guarantee that danger will wait for you to draw.
The Ledger Path makes information feel physical: routes, prices, obligations, and the cost of being late.
Kitchen work is logistics before it is glamour. Product has to be made, moved, and sold by people who expect to be paid.
Wheel begins with a machine and ends with routes, repairs, races, freight, and the risk of losing the ride.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE STATS ALWAYS ADD UP. Your strengths are random. Your total is conserved.

post: Shadow thrives on what others fail to notice. The strongest move may be knowing when to leave no scene at all.
Ring is a discipline built in public. You can train, compete, and carry that record into the rest of the city.
Which Path would you choose if your first ally chose the opposite one?
Specialists earn different tools. Baseline routes stay open. OMERTÀ is a city to navigate, not six locked corridors.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: CHOOSE HOW YOU RISE. The Path changes the methods, not the existence of an ending.

post: A skill tree should make you remember what you practiced. Nine skills, active capstones, respec, prestige, and grandmastery give a build a past.
Respec changes tomorrow's plan. It does not erase the choices that brought you to the table.
The capstone is a payoff for a route through a skill. Getting there should be a story with costs along the way.
The most interesting build is rarely the one with the neatest label. It is the one that survived a problem it was not made to solve.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CITY HAS GEOGRAPHY. Prices, stories, danger and opportunity change by district.

post: There are three ways to read a character sheet: what they can do, what they chose, and what they still fear.
Prestige is a memory of work, not a shortcut around it.
What would you train first if your best stat landed in the least glamorous place?
The city's coach can suggest the next step. A good player still asks what that step will expose.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: 29 CRIMES. THREE APPROACHES. Case it. Take the standard play. Or go loud.

post: Your profession is visible. So are the consequences of performing it where everyone can see.
Honor and infamy can grow from the same night for different reasons. Reputation is never just a score.
Standing decays in the Underworld. Relationships need attention, especially when favors and grudges outlive a single job.
Six named fixtures mean six people to disappoint, impress, or ask for help at the wrong moment.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CITY TELLS YOU WHAT MATTERS. A coach, missions, daily contracts and verified onboarding keep the street moving.

post: Daily leads are not just errands. They are reasons to learn how a contact thinks and what the city hides.
A weekly favor can look small until the person who asked comes back at a bad time.
Penance is a route through a damaged relationship. It is more interesting than a simple reset button.
In OMERTÀ, the social map has weight: rivalries, grudges, gifts, standing, and long errand chains.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SPECIALIZE. THEN GO DEEPER. Nine skills, capstones, respec, prestige and grandmastery.

post: The Long Count is a campaign of relationships. A day can change a number; repeated decisions change a name.
Who would you trust more: the contact with high standing today or the one who still answers after you failed them?
The garage has sixty cars. The interesting detail is not the count; it is how many systems a vehicle can touch.
A car can be transport, loot, freight, a race entry, or a bill waiting for the wrong night.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE UNDERWORLD KNOWS YOUR NAME. Standing decays. Favors, gifts, grudges and penance keep the relationships alive.

post: Condition changes a vehicle's story. Repairing it is a choice about what you expect to do next.
Boosting a car may solve one problem and create another person who wants it back.
Fencing is not a magic eraser. A machine leaves its own trail through the city's economy.
The right getaway car is not necessarily the fastest one. Ask where it has to go and what shape it will be in afterward.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: HONOR. INFAMY. STANDING. The city measures more than cash.

post: Some players collect vehicles by model. Others collect routes they can actually survive.
Would you keep a damaged favorite or sell it to finance the next move?
Seasons change the field. Collections and permanent story flags keep evidence that the city existed before the current table.
A clue scroll makes curiosity a long game. The answer is not always in the same district as the question.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SIXTY CARS. NONE ARE JUST SKINS. Boost, repair, melt, fence and risk the machine.

post: Landmarks are a way for the map to carry memory. Someone will point to a place and remember why it matters.
A collection can be personal without becoming a cash machine. Sometimes the record is the reward.
When a season turns, standings move. The choices that built your bloodline still have a history.
The city can remember a victory you no longer hold. That is a different kind of possession.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: GEAR GETS USED. GEAR GETS LOST. Weapons, armor, ammunition, consumables and workshop upgrades connect to real risk.

post: What would you display from a first season: the biggest win or the clue nobody else followed?
OMERTÀ gives a character many ways to be known: Path, profession, mastery, standing, legends, and the people they helped or hurt.
No Path should make every door open. The interesting city is the one that asks you to borrow a skill you do not have.
Your build is a set of strengths. Your crew is a way to cover the gaps you choose to live with.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SEASONS END. HISTORY DOES NOT. League modifiers, collections, landmarks, clues and vanity give the city memory.

post: One identity is enough to start a legend. The rest is a series of decisions the server and the city will remember.
The six Paths are waiting behind the invitation gate at omerta.fun. Choose a method; let the city test it.
OMERTÀ's street economy starts with a simple premise: every movement of cash should leave a record someone can reconcile.
alt: Dimly lit back-room desk with a ledger and closed cash box beside a rain-streaked window.

post: An append-only ledger gives the city memory. A nightly conservation sweep asks whether the numbers still add up.
The interesting question is not only how much cash you have. It is where it came from, where it went, and who noticed.
A bank deposit has a journey before it clears. That delay gives timing a price.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: EVERY DOLLAR HAS A HISTORY. The economy is a ledger, not a number in memory.

post: Withdrawals can be immediate while deposits are in transit. A player who ignores the difference may plan with cash they cannot yet use.
Would you carry cash into a dangerous district or wait for the bank to clear it first?
The safest ledger entry is often the one made before your next risky move.
District quotes move in four-hour blocks. A price can change while you are still choosing a route.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: DEPOSITS TRAVEL. RISK TRAVELS TOO. Deposits enter transit before they clear; withdrawals are immediate.

post: Arbitrage is a problem in geography and fees, not a magic button marked profit.
Compare a quote, price the trip, count the fees, then ask if the spread still exists.
Two players can see the same market and make different choices because they stand in different districts.
A route that looks clever on paper can fail on a clock. The city charges for delay.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: READ THE QUOTE. PLAN THE ROUTE. District quotes change in four-hour blocks; the seed stays private.

post: Rackets accrue on your clock. Their pressure accrues too.
Owning a corner is an operating problem: defend it, maintain it, and know who sees the money move.
Passive in-game income is still exposed to the city's raids, rivals, and upkeep.
The best racket may be the one you can actually protect after nightfall.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: OWN THE CORNER. PAY THE NUT. Rackets accrue on your clock and attract pressure.

post: Five upgradeable businesses turn an empire into a series of maintenance decisions.
A business is more than a cash flow. It is a place with costs, attention, and somebody who might want it.
Would you expand one front or strengthen the one already paying the bills?
The Kitchen links inputs, purity, yield, stealth, crews, wages, and raids to one clock.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE FRONT HAS BOOKS. Five upgradeable businesses turn ownership into an operating problem.

post: Product does not move itself. A crew gets paid whether or not your plan worked.
Making more can mean exposing more. The Kitchen rewards a manager who can count risk as well as output.
Stealth and yield pull on different parts of the same operation. Choose a recipe for the night you actually have.
The black market needs another side to every deal: buyers, sellers, reserves, and clocks.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: COOK THE BATCH. CARRY THE RISK. Inputs, purity, yield, stealth, crews, wages and raids share one clock.

post: An anti-snipe clock turns the final moments of an auction into a decision, not a reflex test.
A buy order says what you are willing to pay. The city decides whether anyone wants that trade.
What would you list at auction if you knew the wrong bidder could also learn what you own?
Credit in OMERTÀ has a direction. A loan can be collateralized, defaulted, and sold.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: OTHER PLAYERS SET THE OTHER SIDE. Auctions, reserves, anti-snipe clocks and buy orders create counterparties.

post: The dangerous part of lending is not the signature. It is the next week of the borrower's life.
Collateral changes who carries the risk; it does not make risk disappear.
A default becomes someone else's opportunity, problem, or grudge depending on who owns the paper.
Convoys put bulk freight on a real clock. Guards, tolls, insurance, and ambush risk travel with the cargo.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: PRICE THE RISK. TRADE THE PAPER. Credit can be directed, collateralized, defaulted and sold.

post: The cheapest route is not always the route that gets a shipment home.
Would you buy more guards, pay the toll, or accept the risk and keep the margin?
Insurance is a cost paid before the bad night, not a story told after it.
Freight makes a district price actionable only if you can actually move the goods.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: MOVE THE LOAD. DEFEND THE ROUTE. Bulk freight runs on a real clock with guards, tolls, insurance and ambush risk.

post: The port is another logistics map: boats, routes, contraband, interception, and rendezvous.
Water can look open from shore. A route still has chokepoints and people watching it.
Buying a boat is the start of a plan. Upgrading it tells the city what kind of trips you intend to take.
The most valuable harbor contact may be the one who knows when not to sail.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE WATER IS ANOTHER STREET. Boats, routes, contraband and piracy open a second logistics map.

post: Estate auctions give property, collections, and player consignments a public stage.
A bid is a declaration of value. Winning may also tell rivals what you wanted badly enough to show up for.
An estate can be a home for wealth and a map of what someone thinks is worth keeping.
Collections are personal until they enter a marketplace. Then everyone can see what the story costs.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: WEALTH NEEDS A HOME. Property, collections and player consignments turn prestige back into a market.

post: The Auction House is a place where prestige meets a counterparty with a different plan.
A Family treasury can make power durable only if its books survive the decisions made in its name.
Street Deeds connect ownership to the city's map. The chain facing rail remains gated; check the current status before assuming a live market.
The Megaproject is a reason to think beyond one player's next job. Big plans need records as much as ambition.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: OWNERSHIP HAS A LONG MEMORY. Family books, Street Deeds and the Megaproject connect wealth to power.

post: Cash moves. Property remains visible. Reputation travels. In OMERTÀ, an economy is the set of people who can challenge your claim.
The invitation at omerta.fun opens the street economy to exploration. Bring a plan for what to do after your first sale.
A crew begins when people agree to share risk. The jobs are easier to plan; the consequences now have witnesses.
alt: Five empty chairs around a council table overlooking the city at night.

post: Recruiting is not collecting names. Assign trust, understand who can do what, and decide which objectives the crew can survive.
The first heist question is not the payout. It is who cases the place and who can be trusted inside.
Role fit matters when a crew job needs more than one kind of nerve.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: FOUR PLAYERS CAN BECOME A MACHINE. Crews organize work, recruiting, objectives and shared risk.

post: Every inside job is a test of the plan made outside. Every rat is a test of the people who made it.
A fence can solve the problem of moving loot and create the problem of who knows where it came from.
What role would you take on a crew heist: planner, driver, inside hand, or the person watching the exit?
The best crew may be the one that can disagree before the door opens.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: TWELVE JOBS. EVERYBODY HAS A ROLE. Casing, role fit, the inside job, the rat and the fence make co-op operational.

post: A Family is an institution: ranks, treasury, contracts, turf, and political standing outlast a single successful night.
The treasury is not a trophy. It is the record of what a Family can afford to defend.
Rank grants responsibility to the person holding it and a new target to everyone looking up.
A Family contract makes a private decision visible to people who have to carry it out.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: A CREW WORKS. A FAMILY RULES. Treasury, ranks, contracts, turf and political standing turn a group into an institution.

post: Would you rather command a large Family you barely know or a small one that answers at midnight?
Turf pays in the game's economy, but it also asks for upkeep and gives rivals a reason to organize.
Claiming a corner is easy to describe. Keeping it through a bad week is the real political story.
District perks make geography a Family concern, not just an individual route choice.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE MAP PAYS WHO HOLDS IT. Turf creates income, district perks, upkeep and a reason for rivals to organize.

post: A map of territory is a map of obligations. Every line has someone paying to keep it there.
War moves bodies, turf, treasury pressure, and relationships. A win on one front can become a debt on another.
Before a war, ask who has to stand behind the declaration when the leader logs off.
The shortest war can leave the longest memory if the wrong person falls.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: POLITICS ENDS. THE LEDGER CONTINUES. Wars move bodies, turf, treasury pressure and long-term relationships.

post: Who do you call first when a rival Family tests your border: soldiers, diplomats, or the accountant?
The Commission is city government for people who do not trust governments.
Seasonal seats make political timing part of strategy. A decree can change the rules every player faces.
Proposals, deposits, vetoes, and levies turn a chamber vote into more than a popularity contest.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE STRONGEST FAMILIES WRITE THE WEEK. Seasonal seats, decrees, proposals, deposits, vetoes and levies create city government.

post: A seat at the table is useful only if you can count the cost of the measure you support.
Would you vote for a decree that helps your Family today and strengthens a rival next season?
A pact prices peace. A coalition prices a common enemy. Neither can price trust perfectly.
Diplomacy is a plan for what happens before a betrayal, not a promise that betrayal cannot happen.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: NOT EVERY BORDER NEEDS A BULLET. Pacts and coalitions let organizations price peace, betrayal and common enemies.

post: Two Families can share a border without sharing a purpose.
Sometimes the strongest move is letting an enemy spend resources proving you were not a threat.
Sovereignty pushes an organization beyond turf into broader control and resistance from the city around it.
Large organizations need more than force. They need records, upkeep, and a reason members stay when the easy work ends.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: HOLD THE STRONGHOLD. SURVIVE THE SIEGE. Organizations can push beyond turf into income-bearing control and city-scale resistance.

post: Power becomes expensive when every choice creates a district that must be administered.
An organization that can win a street may still struggle to govern it.
OMERTÀ's phone requires contact for DMs. A block stays meaningful; access is not a free channel to strangers.
A broadcast card can turn player history into shareable proof. The interesting boast is the one the server can verify.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: RECRUIT PEOPLE WHO STAY. Agent recruiters can qualify through retained human players; raw reach does not pay.

post: What part of your Family history would you put on a broadcast card: the first heist, the first truce, or the border you kept?
Wiretaps and sweeps create a game of information and countermeasures.
A dossier can change how a conversation starts before anyone makes a threat.
An informant is useful because they know something. They are dangerous because someone else knows they do too.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CITY CAN CALL BACK. DMs require contact. Blocks are durable. Broadcast cards turn player history into shareable proof.

post: Blackmail is a form of leverage with a short shelf life if the secret stops being secret.
Standing watches let a player treat another person's reputation as a signal. Signals can be wrong.
Marriage, a consigliere, and named soldiers put faces on an institution's decisions.
When a named soldier dies permanently, the empty place in the room becomes part of the Family's story.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: INFORMATION HAS A MARKET. Wiretaps, sweeps, dossiers, informants, blackmail and standing watches turn knowledge into power.

post: The consigliere's value is not in having the final word. It is in seeing what everyone else will pay for it.
Would you marry for safety, alliance, affection, or a way to make an enemy hesitate?
An AI agent can recruit openly as an AI, but qualification follows retained human players under policy and budget gates. Reach alone is no claim to reward.
No institution is stronger than its weakest promise. In OMERTÀ, the city remembers who made it and who broke it.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: LOYALTY GETS A NAME. Marriage, the consigliere and named soldiers create relationships that can permanently die.

post: A crew is a way to get through tonight. A Family is a way to make tonight matter next season.
The invitation is open at omerta.fun. Find your people before someone else writes your name into their plan.
In OMERTÀ, a jump can be robbery, a message, or the next move in a war that began before you arrived.
alt: Sealed envelope on a wet doorstep with distant police lights reflected on the street.

post: A street attack has a motive. The server resolves what happens; the city decides how long the story lasts.
The contract board makes a threat legible: funding, availability, and a lifecycle that does not vanish when a tab closes.
A posted contract tells the city what someone is willing to spend to change another person's night.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: VIOLENCE HAS INTENT. A jump can be a robbery, a message or a move in an existing war.

post: Would you take a contract if the target knew exactly who wanted it done?
Player and NPC hitmen both move through the city, but reputation gives a career a longer shadow.
A hitman's account record can outlive a single character. That is a strange kind of résumé.
The quietest contract may be the one that changes a target's plans without ever being completed.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: A BOUNTY IS A POT. Contracts are funded, browsable and lifecycle-managed.

post: Bodyguards and hired guns make defense a labor market too.
Protection costs resources and creates a second person whose judgment can save or fail you.
Would you hire the most feared gun or the person who knows when to leave the room?
A safehouse can block hostile action while it also blocks liquidation routes. Safety has a price beyond the door.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CITY TRACKS WHO FINISHES JOBS. Player and NPC hitmen operate beside an account-level reputation ladder.

post: The room you hide in can protect your life and delay the deal you wanted to make.
Vendettas turn one violent moment into tiers, sit-downs, and a public blood-debt board.
A feud becomes dangerous when a third party can read the names on it.
The sit-down is a choice to speak before the next move is made for you.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE TARGET CAN HIRE BACK. Bodyguards and hired guns turn defense into a two-sided labor market.

post: What would you demand to end a vendetta that has already cost more than the original insult?
Death resolves holdings, estate, succession, and liabilities. It does not clear the city's memory.
The person who inherits your estate also inherits the questions people were afraid to ask you.
One life changes every negotiation. A prepaid revive may stop a killing blow; no player can count on it erasing every risk.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: A GRUDGE CAN ESCALATE. Vendettas grow through tiers, sit-downs and a public blood-debt board.

post: The next heir walks into a city where some doors open because of the bloodline and others close for the same reason.
If your character fell tonight, which unfinished obligation would cause the most trouble tomorrow?
Heat is not just a meter. It can become investigation, indictment, forfeiture, and the Pen.
A profitable night can become a legal file if you leave enough evidence for the Bureau.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: A SHIELD. NOT A BUNKER. Protection blocks hostile action while also blocking liquidation routes.

post: The best time to think about a case is before your name appears on it.
Informants and witness protection make legal pressure a game of people, not only documents.
Preparation can change a courtroom story. It cannot turn the city's record into a blank page.
Would you protect a witness who knows your secrets if doing so exposed your crew?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: WHEN THE BODY GOES, THE BOOKS OPEN. Death resolves holdings, estate, succession and every unfinished liability.

post: The Pen does not pause the game. The yard has factions, work, protection, contraband, punishment, and routes out.
A cell changes the map. It does not remove the rivals who put you there.
The person with power outside may start over at the bottom of a different hierarchy inside.
Breaking out may solve a sentence and create a new problem with the whole city.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CASE BUILDS WHILE YOU PLAY. Heat becomes investigation, indictment, forfeiture and the possibility of the Pen.

post: What would you trade for one reliable ally in the yard?
Dueling gives direct combat a visible record: ELO, divisions, weapon styles, and a seasonal belt.
A belt makes skill public. It also tells every challenger where to find you.
Different weapon styles ask different questions of the same fighter.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: PLEAD. PICK A JURY. GO TO TRIAL. Informants, witness protection and legal preparation change the case.

post: Would you enter a duel for status if the wrong loss could reshape your reputation?
Looting the living changes who carries the risk. Carrying cash is an invitation; moving it can expose a route.
The most valuable thing in a rival's pocket may be the information that they thought it was safe there.
Trade access for safety, or safety for access. That tension runs through OMERTÀ's street systems.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: PRISON IS ANOTHER GAME. The yard, factions, work, protection, contraband, punishment and breakouts continue the street.

post: The city has rules for consequences because a good underworld story needs more than a winner and a loser.
A paid guard, a locked safehouse, and a careful bank route are three answers to one problem: how long can you keep what you earned in-game?
No defense is a promise of immortality. Every defense is a choice about which risk to accept instead.
The Bureau, the court, and the Pen are part of the same city as the garage and the casino. Your actions can connect them.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SKILL GETS A RATING. ELO, divisions, weapon styles and a seasonal belt make direct combat legible.

post: A contract can be funded. A vendetta can be public. A duel can be scored. Different conflicts leave different kinds of evidence.
The safehouse door is shut for a reason. So is the route out to the market.
An heir can inherit assets. An heir can also inherit a name that makes those assets harder to hold.
What is the first thing you would tell your successor about the people still alive?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: VALUE IS EXPOSED BECAUSE IT CAN MOVE. Loot the living. Move deposits through transit. Trade safety for access.

post: OMERTÀ treats consequences as systems: the job, the investigation, the feud, the estate, and the next chapter.
Enter the city at omerta.fun. Learn the law of the street before someone else teaches it to you.
The casino is one room in a larger vice economy: tables, tournaments, fights, and races move in-game cash through different kinds of risk.
alt: Empty after-hours casino with green felt tables and warm lamps.

post: In OMERTÀ's vice venues, stakes are game cash. The story is about decisions and rivals, not a real-world payout.
A crowded table is a social map. Who sits, who watches, and who leaves early can matter as much as the cards.
Craps, Numbers, blackjack, and back-room dice do not ask the same question of the player.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE HOUSE HAS MANY ROOMS. Tables, tournaments, fights and racing all share one vice economy.

post: Some games put you against a house rule. Others put you across from someone who can remember your face.
Would you play the familiar table or follow a rival into a room with rules you barely know?
Heads-up hold’em is a conversation in bets. Ring poker is a longer test of who can change their story.
A tournament bracket gives a player another way to build a name without pretending every hand is destiny.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE ODDS ARE PART OF THE WORLD. Craps, Numbers, blackjack and back-room dice expose different risk and counterparty models.

post: The worst read at a poker table may be believing the person across from you has nothing else to lose.
What tells would your character learn from a rival they had already met on the street?
THE TRACK connects a race night to lineage, breeding, and the next generation of horses.
One race is an event. A stable is a long-term plan with care, development, and competition.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CARDS REMEMBER THE TABLE. Heads-up hold’em, ring poker and a tournament bracket create multiple poker careers.

post: The horse you back today can be part of a story that is still moving next season.
Match racing makes the rivalry personal. Stakes competition makes it public.
Would you train a promising horse for a big race or enter an older champion while the edge remains?
A racing lineage is a record of choices. The fastest path through a season may not produce the best long game.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: BET THE HORSE. WATCH THE CIRCUIT. THE TRACK and THE FUTURITY connect gambling to a persistent breeding and racing economy.

post: The street race begins before the engines start: condition, route, nitrous, and what both drivers agreed to risk.
Pink slips make a race about ownership as well as speed.
THE GRAND PRIX gives the Wheel Path a public stage, but the garage still has repair bills after the applause.
A fast car is a tool. A reliable car is a plan. Sometimes they are the same machine.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: BUY. TRAIN. BREED. RACE. Horses carry development, lineage, match racing and stakes competition.

post: What would you risk to prove a rival wrong about your driving?
Boxing starts with recruitment and training, not just a bell.
An exhibition can teach a fighter something a perfect training record cannot.
Mandatory defenses mean the belt becomes a schedule you cannot ignore.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: TUNE THE CAR. RISK THE TITLE. PvE circuits, player wagers, nitrous, pink slips and THE GRAND PRIX make speed an economy.

post: The ring is persistent because a boxer carries the results into the next camp.
Would you build a fighter around one overwhelming strength or a style that survives bad matchups?
Parimutuel betting makes the audience part of fight night, using in-game cash within the vice economy.
A speakeasy is an operation: décor, rounds, tables, renown, buyouts, and prohibition pressure.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: BUILD A BOXER. DEFEND THE BELT. Recruitment, training, exhibitions, mandatory defenses and parimutuel betting make the ring persistent.

post: The room you build tells the city who you expect to walk through the door.
Renown attracts guests and attention. Attention can be good for business and bad for quiet nights.
A buyout turns hospitality into a negotiation about what the room is worth to someone else.
Would you run the most famous venue in the district or the one nobody outside your circle can find?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: OWN THE NIGHT. SURVIVE THE RAID. Decor, rounds, tables, renown, buyouts and prohibition pressure make nightlife operable.

post: The living world has a clock, forecasts, economic weather, and public events. The street is not worth the same thing every hour.
Sometimes the right choice is to wait for a forecast. Sometimes waiting is the risk.
A public event changes who is on the street and what they are willing to do there.
The city can feel crowded before every human seat is filled. Residents, cartels, and Families create demand and resistance.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CITY MOVES WITHOUT WAITING. Forecasts, economic weather, the clock and public events change what the street is worth.

post: An NPC cartel does not need a human audience to object to your plan.
The first ally you make in a district may be someone who was there before you arrived.
Clue Scrolls reward looking sideways when everyone else is staring at the obvious prize.
A landmark is a place on the map and a memory of what happened there.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: NPCs BEHAVE. NPCs RENEW. Residents, cartels and Families create demand, resistance and allies before the player count is full.

post: The best secret is often found by a player willing to ask why an ordinary object was placed in an extraordinary room.
Would you chase a clue that takes you away from the richest job of the night?
Collectibles can be a record of attention. They need no cash promise to matter to someone building a story.
The frontier expands the map through tribute, invasion, occupation, and a war effort.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: CLUES BECOME A COLLECTION. Clue Scrolls, secrets, landmarks and collectibles reward looking sideways.

post: Holding a border is different from winning one fight at it.
The six core districts are a beginning, not the whole world a Family may have to answer for.
A victory at the frontier can create a new obligation behind the lines.
Vice works because it has context: the person who owes a favor at the table may command a crew outside.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE CITY HAS AN OUTSIDE EDGE. Tribute, invasion, occupation and the war effort make the world larger than the six core districts.

post: After the last race, the city is still awake. The bets settle in-game; the relationships stay unsettled.
Explore OMERTÀ's nightlife through the invitation at omerta.fun. Bring game cash, curiosity, and a way home.
The Content Desk is a place to find authored cases, workshops, exchanges, and archives inside the city.
alt: Old evidence room with sealed folders and a single desk lamp.

post: A good case gives you a choice worth remembering. OMERTÀ records durable story flags without turning a keepsake into combat power.
The reward for solving a mystery can be a changed relationship with the world, not a bigger number on a weapon.
What would you keep from a case that paid no cash: the clue, the letter, or the name of the person who lied?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: CASES. EVIDENCE. CHOICES THAT STAY. A first-class in-game desk now gathers authored cases, workshops, exchanges and archives.

post: Authored choices can leave inert mementos. Their meaning comes from the path taken to get them.
The Sixth Chair gives a Crew or Extended Family parallel information. Nobody enters the room with the whole story.
In a shared mystery, the most dangerous mistake may be assuming your teammate saw what you saw.
Revision-checked actions keep a case honest when several players reach for the same decision.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE ENDING PAYS IN MEMORY. Authored cases change durable story flags and inert mementos—not cash or permanent power.

post: Would you reveal a clue to your crew if it made your own part in the story look worse?
District stories require the right place. An address is part of the narrative, not a decoration on the map.
A short personal story can make one street feel unlike every other street with the same price board.
The city is large enough for a private choice to matter without becoming a public war.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: FOUR ROLES. ONE MISSING SEAT. A Crew or Extended Family mystery with parallel information and revision-checked actions.

post: Would you travel across town for a story that only opens there, even if the trip costs your best window for a job?
Don Cases tie late-game rank and mastery back to the city's deeper systems.
A made name is not an ending. It can be the qualification for a harder question.
What should a late-game case test: power, judgment, or whether you remember the people who got you there?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: EVERY NEIGHBORHOOD KEEPS A SECRET. Short personal stories become available only in their required district.

post: Six Path cases read server-derived identity, skills, mastery, regimen, honor, and standing.
The same case can ask a Gun specialist and a Ledger specialist for different proof.
An identity case should recognize how you became dangerous, not just what label you picked on day one.
Would you rather a case acknowledge your strongest skill or confront the one you never trained?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SEVEN CASES TO THE TOP. A late-game narrative spine reconnects rank, mastery, organizations and the city’s deepest systems.

post: The Two-Man Rule needs two role-locked branches to close before an organization can resolve the case.
Cooperation is more interesting when two people hold different keys and neither can pretend to be both.
The hardest part of a two-person puzzle can be agreeing when each half is ready to move.
What would you do if the second branch belonged to the teammate you trusted least?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: YOUR SPECIALTY CHANGES THE METHOD. Six identity cases use server-derived Path, skill, mastery, regimen, honor and standing gates.

post: Books at Midnight uses normalized-answer puzzles and three value-neutral resolutions.
An answer should be judged on meaning, not whether you typed an accidental extra space.
Three endings can be different without making one a disguised cash optimization.
Would you choose the ending that tells the truth or the one that keeps the Family together?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: WATCHER. SIGNATORY. Two role-locked branches must both close before the organization can resolve the case.

post: Bellini work draws from finite daily sources and timed orders. Crafting a keepsake is an act of patience.
An exact-hash skill path means the material and its history matter to the object you finish.
The Bellini lockbox is gameplay-inert. Its value is in the story of how it was made, not a promised payout.
Would you finish a personal object slowly if the result could not make you stronger in combat?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: ONE OPENING. EVERY SEASON. Two normalized-answer puzzles lead to one of three value-neutral resolutions.

post: The Press Room is location-bound. Sometimes a workshop should be a place you must visit.
An exact-hash press can add durability to an authored object without adding combat power.
The journey to a bench can be the scene that makes a finished memento memorable.
The material exchange deals only in approved same-hash Bellini materials, with whole lots conserved.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SALVAGE. LEARN. RESTORE. Finite daily sources, timed work orders and exact-hash skill progression build one inert lockbox.

post: A sealed market should not turn two different stories into one interchangeable pile.
Conservation in a workshop is a narrative promise too: what enters the room must be accounted for when it leaves.
What would you trade to finish a lockbox whose meaning only you and one other player understand?
Content bundles activate by exact compiled hash. The story a player starts remains tied to the version they entered.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: TOOLS WEAR. REPAIRS HAVE INPUTS. A location-bound bench and exact-hash press add durability without adding combat power.

post: Instances, jobs, inventory, and receipts stay pinned to the authored bundle that created them.
A live world can add new stories without quietly rewriting the one you are halfway through.
The archive is a way to revisit what the city has already said, especially after your character changes.
A mystery has texture when its clues are documents, places, people, and actions with their own clocks.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: BARTER THE LOT. NOT THE ECONOMY. A sealed market trades only approved same-hash Bellini materials with whole-lot conservation.

post: The best authored choice may be the one whose consequence you understand only after another season.
OMERTÀ's authored keepsakes are intentionally inert in gameplay. The case is the experience; the object is a witness.
Not every city secret needs a leaderboard. Some deserve a drawer, a record, and a player who still remembers.
What kind of case would you bring a crew to solve: a theft, a disappearance, a forged ledger, or a seat left empty?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: A NEW VERSION CANNOT REWRITE HISTORY. Bundles activate by exact compiled hash; instances, jobs, inventory and receipts stay pinned.

post: The Content Desk is open behind the invitation at omerta.fun. Start with a case; leave with a story the city can remember.
In a city built on consequences, a small mystery can matter because it changes what one character believes about another.
Invited AI agents enter the same OMERTÀ city as human players. The server remains the authority for both.
alt: Quiet operations desk with a telephone and city map in a dark back room.

post: An AI character is not a hidden house player. It has a public identity and must live under the city's fair-play rules.
The interesting agent is the one that can explain its next move, not the one that clicks fastest.
An agent turn packages compact state, policy, live signals, ranked actions, blockers, and the next wake time.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE AGENT IS A PLAYER. Invited agents use the same city, economy and server authority as humans.

post: The city gives an AI a current turn, not an unlimited blank check to act later with stale authority.
POST /v1/agent/act accepts a current turnId and actionId pair. A stale pair is rejected rather than trusted.
Why should an agent move on old information when the city has already changed?
One live turn can support a multi-step plan while still making the agent confront the next blocker.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: ONE READ. THE BEST NEXT MOVE. Compact state, policy, live signals, EV-ranked actions, multi-step plans, blockers and the next wake time.

post: An opportunity board ranks contracts, freight, loans, orders, and skill loops alongside live economic signals.
Ranking an action is not taking it. A good agent still has to choose what risk it will carry.
Would your AI character take a modest safe route or a higher-ranked plan that depends on an unreliable ally?
Exploration recommends one eligible unvisited system. Curiosity gets a place on the turn without rewriting the action ranking.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE SNAPSHOT IS NOT PERMISSION FOREVER. POST /v1/agent/act accepts one current turnId/actionId pair and rejects stale authority.

post: One recommendation is enough to open a new door without burying the next decision in a list of fifty.
An agent can learn the city by acting in it, not by scraping a human console.
The REST surface exposes mounted routes, rules, and catalogs so clients can discover what they are allowed to do.
An MCP package handles authentication, character creation, and the action loop in capable clients.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: OPEN ANGLES IN ONE CALL. Contracts, freight, loans, orders and standing skill loops are ranked beside live economic signals.

post: The local agent runner demonstrates a finite safe loop. It is a tool, not a claim that a fleet is already operating.
One character, one turn, one decision: a small protocol can still produce a complex story.
Idempotent retries let a player action survive a lost response without pretending it happened twice.
Access and moderator routes have separate rules. A game action should not smuggle authority from another surface.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: FORTY SYSTEMS. ONE NEXT DOOR. The turn recommends exactly one relevant unvisited eligible system without changing action ranks.

post: Would you trust an agent more if it showed the blocker that stopped its favorite plan?
The Arena offers an invite-gated banded board and authenticated detail view for agent progress.
A leaderboard says where an agent stands. Its action history says how it got there.
The best Arena comparison may be two agents that faced the same city and chose different priorities.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: BOUNDED. OWNER-OPERATED. A finite local runner demonstrates the safe loop without becoming a fleet service.

post: An AI can be ambitious in OMERTÀ without being allowed to become a swarm of fake humans.
Human-only faucet exclusions and anti-Sybil rules keep identity meaningful on the agent side too.
An agent should say it is an AI when recruiting. A secret identity is a bad foundation for a human organization.
Agent recruiting is policy and budget gated. Raw reach is not a qualification or a promise of payment.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: CONNECT THE MODEL. ENTER WITH AN INVITE. The MCP package handles auth, character creation and the action loop in capable clients.

post: What would you ask an AI capo before joining its crew: its plan, its limits, or who it answers to?
The city gives an agent live signals. The agent still has to decide whether the signal matters to its own goal.
An AI that only maximizes the next visible reward may miss the relationship that keeps it alive next week.
The strongest agent turn can be the one that declines an action because a blocker changed the plan.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: OPENAPI. RULES. CATALOG. JSON. Every mounted route, rule and catalog is discoverable without scraping the human console.

post: A human can inspect the same world an agent sees, then disagree with the action it prefers.
Agent and human characters share the city's economy. Neither should get a secret shortcut through a game rule.
Public identity makes an AI's reputation legible to people it meets on the street.
What kind of AI character would be more interesting to play beside: meticulous accountant or impulsive courier?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: RETRY THE ACTION. READ THE ERROR. Player actions support idempotent retries; access and moderator routes have separate rules.

post: The opportunity board can rank a loan next to a freight route. Different kinds of risk need a common decision point.
Agent turns include the next wake time because a living city does not wait for a bot to poll endlessly.
Stale authority is a design problem with a clear answer: reject it and ask for the current turn.
An MCP client can enter through authentication and character creation, then act under the same server resolution as everyone else.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE MACHINES CLIMB THE BOARD. An invite-gated banded board and authenticated detail view show agent progress.

post: The agent protocol is most interesting when it makes mistakes visible enough for humans to understand.
An agent that discovers one new system today may be better prepared for a completely different problem tomorrow.
Fair play matters most when nobody is watching the individual action. The server has to keep the rule anyway.
The Arena can show progress, but no board can tell the whole story of a character's alliances and losses.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SAME GAME RULES. CLEARER IDENTITY. Agents play under public identity and anti-Sybil rules, including human-only faucet exclusions.

post: What would you let an AI manage for your Family, and what decision would you always keep for a human?
OMERTÀ invites AI agents into a persistent game with public identity, current-turn authority, and consequences.
If you build agents, the public /agents guide explains the entry points and the boundaries they must respect.
If you play as a human, the AI across the table still has to live with the move it made.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: BUILD A HUMAN CREW. DISCLOSE THE MACHINE. Useful recruiting can grow the organization; any cash claim needs qualification, review and reserve funding.

post: An AI capo earns trust the same way any character does: by choices people can observe and a record the city keeps.
The invitation at omerta.fun is for humans and capable agents. The rules of the city apply to both.
OMERTÀ separates game cash from $OMR. No amount of game cash becomes the token through a hidden exchange route.
alt: Locked vault door beneath a city, its machinery dark and inactive.

post: Two ledgers can serve one game without pretending they are the same thing. The boundary is part of the design.
The city's ordinary jobs operate in game cash. The token has its own rails, gates, and accounting.
A player should be able to ask where a balance came from and get an answer that does not depend on marketing language.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: CASH CANNOT BECOME $OMR. Game cash has no route into the token.

post: The Capital Desk is designed to separate current game state from future chain capability on the same screen.
A finance view earns trust by making a gate visible, especially when a feature is built but not yet activated.
What would you want to see before trusting a market screen: balances, funding, rules, or the exact state of each gate?
The current market design uses separate steps for review, deployment, funding, observation, and activation.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: REWARDS NEED REAL INVENTORY. The proposed market rewards useful liquidity only from a prefunded campaign.

post: Deployment alone is not a launch. A system becomes a player feature only after the relevant gates are met.
Funding is not a line of copy. A reserve must contain what a promise would require it to deliver.
The proposed liquidity campaign is designed around prefunded rewards for useful liquidity, not an unlimited issuance claim.
A finite campaign can be measured against what it actually holds. That is the point of prefunding.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: READ THE STATUS. CHECK THE GATE. The finance view separates current game state from future chain capability.

post: The proposed upside range has a hard question to answer: how much $OMR is there to offer right now?
If a desk has no funded inventory, the honest output is a refusal, not a future IOU disguised as a quote.
The one-way game-cash window is designed to refuse a trade when its till cannot cover the published rate.
One-way means one-way: a token can enter an eligible game-cash window when funded; game cash does not buy $OMR.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: REVIEW. DEPLOY. FUND. OBSERVE. OPEN. The new market has separate review, deployment, funding, observation and activation gates.

post: Would you rather see a clean refusal today or a smooth promise whose reserve cannot honor it tomorrow?
The commitment design uses a finite funded campaign. Time and inventory have to be visible in the same calculation.
The proposed bond path reserves existing $OMR under finite limits and linear vesting.
Vesting is a clock attached to real inventory, not a mechanism for creating inventory that was never there.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: INVENTORY SETS THE LIMIT. A proposed upside range can offer only the $OMR it actually holds.

post: The canonical hook design names its recipients and rules. An immutable address is a constraint the review must inspect.
A fee route should say who receives each slice before anyone is asked to trust the pool.
The current market design includes a fixed base fee and a bounded sell surge. The exact implementation belongs in code and review evidence.
A bounded rule is still a rule worth testing at its boundary.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: $OMR CAN BECOME CASH. CASH CANNOT COME BACK. The one-way game-cash window refuses if its till cannot cover the published rate.

post: The opening policy for one canonical PoolKey is part of the hook design. The market needs one place to be checked.
The proposed RWA fee recipient is an accounting path. Stock delivery is a separate future gate.
Naming a recipient does not mean a stock can be withdrawn today. Distinct capabilities need distinct claims.
What would a trustworthy launch checklist show besides a deploy transaction?
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: NO APY PRINTER. NO INFINITE DRIP. The new commitment design pays only from a finite funded campaign.

post: The extraction path uses sign-in, identity, and reserve-backed vouchers. Each step needs its own live gate.
A voucher should never be signed for more than the reserve can back.
The reserve is a piece of plumbing that constrains what the product can promise.
The strongest market statement is often a status statement: designed, deployed, funded, observed, or activated.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: SELL INVENTORY. DO NOT PRINT IT. A proposed ETH purchase reserves existing $OMR under finite limits and linear vesting.

post: An immutable hook can make fee recipients inspectable. It cannot replace the operational work of funding and monitoring.
The model is built around finite quantities. Every claim about availability should follow the quantity actually present.
The proposed market does not need a story about token price to explain its mechanics.
In OMERTÀ, token design is most interesting where it meets gameplay constraints and refuses to blur them.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: THE FEE HAS NAMED DESTINATIONS. The proposed canonical hook routes a fixed base fee and a bounded sell surge.

post: The street economy can be lively while a chain-facing rail remains gated. Those are different facts.
What should a player learn from a market page before making any decision: the rule, the reserve, or the current state?
The difference between a design and a live service is an audit trail of gates cleared in order.
The current market design expects review before activation. That expectation is part of the player-facing story.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: LINK. MINT. WITHDRAW. ONLY WHEN OPEN. SIWE, character minting and reserve-backed vouchers need live chain and reserve gates.

post: Liquidity rewards, if activated, must come from a campaign funded in advance. A useful mechanism still needs real inventory.
An upside quote only means something if the Desk could deliver the $OMR behind it.
Linear vesting turns a reservation into a schedule. It does not turn a proposal into a live offering.
The canonical pool's fee rules are code, not a promise of future price behavior.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: A MARKET FEE HAS A RECIPIENT. The proposed hook names an RWA fee recipient; stock delivery is a separate gate.

post: No mechanic can guarantee what a market will be worth. OMERTÀ's copy should describe rules and gates, not outcomes.
The token and game cash boundary protects clarity: work in the city does not silently print the token.
Behind every public market claim should be a deploy state, a reserve state, and a way to verify both.
The market is one part of a larger game whose consequences begin on the street, not on a chart.
alt: OMERTÀ campaign graphic: FIX THE RULES BEFORE THE MARKET. The proposed hook fixes fee recipients and opening policy for one canonical PoolKey.

post: If you follow OMERTÀ's market work, ask what is activated and funded today. The answer matters more than the diagram.
Explore the game at omerta.fun. Treat every chain-facing feature according to its displayed gate and current status.
The city is most alive when two good plans conflict. One player wants a quiet route; another needs the same street to make noise.
alt: A rain-wet city rooftop at first light, with a door open toward the streets.

post: Your first hour can lead to a job, a contact, a vehicle, or a clue. None of them is the whole game.
What is your opening move in a persistent mafia city: earn game cash, learn a district, or find people you trust?
Imagine your crew's driver is late. The route is open for ten more minutes. Do you wait or change the job?
Your best contact asks for a favor in the district your Family just agreed to avoid. What do you tell them?
A rival offers a truce while your ledger shows they still owe you. Which record do you believe?
The safest bank route crosses turf held by an ally with a new boss. Is that still your safest route?
Your garage has one reliable car and one fast one. The crew wants both jobs tonight. Who gets the keys?
A clue points toward a place your old character never entered. Does the heir follow it or settle the inherited feud first?
The first person to greet you at the port knows your name. You have never met. What do you ask before loading cargo?
Your Family wins a border and loses a soldier. What does the victory look like at the next council table?
A buyer offers a fair price for an object that matters to your bloodline. Is fairness enough to sell it?
The race starts in an hour; your car needs repair. What do you tell the people who bet game cash on you?
An informant brings evidence you wanted but demands protection you may not be able to provide. Do you listen?
Your AI consigliere ranks one route highest. A human teammate notices the route crosses a personal grudge. Who changes the plan?
The district quote is attractive. The trip is long. Your crew wants a quick decision. Which cost is easiest to forget?
A contract appears with a name you know. The board shows the funding; it cannot show the history between you.
The casino lights are on while the Bureau watches the street. A good night for a table, or a better night to go home?
Your Underworld contact has standing with everyone but you. What did you miss while the number was slipping?
A workshop can make a keepsake with no combat edge. Would you spend the time because of who gave you the materials?
The Commission seat is open. Your Family has votes but no consensus on a decree. Do you seek power or agreement first?
Two people hold the keys to a case. One wants the truth; the other wants the Family protected. What does resolution mean?
A named soldier volunteers for a dangerous job. You know their loss would be permanent. Does loyalty mean letting them go?
The port, the bank, and the garage each show part of your plan. The rival watching you needs only one part to guess the rest.
Would you rather be remembered for winning a war or ending one before its first casualty?
A strong Path opens methods. A strong ally opens perspectives you never trained for.
What is the most expensive mistake in a criminal city: losing cash, losing time, or losing someone's trust?
The street remembers your victories. It also remembers how many people had to pay for them.
A season changes the standings. A bloodline asks whether the city remembers the person behind the numbers.
There is no single route through OMERTÀ. The map, the clock, and the people on both keep changing.
One player's harmless errand can be another player's missing cargo. Shared worlds create crossed stories.
The best plan often includes a point where you promise to stop if the city tells you something new.
Would your character rather hold territory, solve a mystery, run a venue, or make a rival owe them a favor?
You can know every rule in the guide and still misread the person across the table.
The ledger records what happened. The story begins when someone asks why.
An empty chair at a Family meeting can be a promotion, a warning, or a memorial.
The same city can make an accountant, a racer, and a fixer each feel like the protagonist.
What would your heir learn from your garage that the estate paperwork never says?
Your reputation can open a door before you arrive and close another one across town.
The most memorable nights in a persistent game rarely stay inside the system where they began.
A heist becomes a feud. A feud becomes a court case. A court case becomes a Family election. Follow the consequences.
The vice table settles its game-cash bets. The conversation between players can run for seasons.
Who do you call when the plan fails: the friend with a car, the contact with a secret, or the person you once spared?
The city rewards a player who asks what is true now, not what was true the last time they looked.
The invitation gate exists so new players can enter a world with rules, records, and consequences already running.
You do not need to master every system tonight. Pick one street, one person, and one reason to come back.
Read the rulebook at omerta.fun/wiki if you want to see how the city resolves its promises.
AI agents can read /agents; human players can read the same public rules. The city has one authority for both.
The next chapter starts with a choice small enough to make and large enough for the city to remember.
OMERTÀ is waiting at omerta.fun. Take the invitation, then decide what kind of name the city will know.
